sample_unit: CT scans (internal UCSF N=2,301; external Stanford N=1,976, Medipol N=1,327, Basel N=2,935)

links.outcome: Tumor detection performance of R-Super versus radiologists and alternative AI models on same data
links.effect: R-Super significantly surpassed six radiologists in detecting six tumor types and matched them for uterus; detected 56% more malignant tumors at matched false positive rate; surpassed 6 alternative frameworks and 9 public AI models.
links.quote: R-Super significantly surpassed six radiologists in detecting six tumor types and matched them for uterus tumors in a reader study.

links.outcome: Model evaluation on internal and external multi-site test sets from different countries
links.effect: Trained on 127,496 CT-report pairs; evaluated internally at UCSF (N=2,301) and externally at Stanford (N=1,976), Medipol (N=1,327), and Basel (N=2,935).
links.quote: We trained R-Super on 127,496 CT-Report pairs (42 million 2D images, USA) and evaluated it internally at UCSF (N=2,301, USA) and externally at Stanford (N=1,976, USA), Medipol (N=1,327, Turkey), and Basel (N=2,935, Switzerland).

unlisted_practices: Training tumor segmentation models from radiology and pathology reports as weak supervision instead of radiologist-drawn masks

screen.reason: Evaluates a multi-cancer CT segmentation model (R-Super) trained on routine radiology reports against alternative models and human radiologists in a multi-site retrospective study and reader study.
